eli: heads-up — saw a weird perf/regression when enabling INT8 KV on long-context streaming. p95 jumped on small batches. :thinking:

maria: details? perf numbers?

eli: running quick A/B on 13B model (16k context). Baseline FP16 KV: p95 85ms, mem per-shard ~1.6GB. INT8 KV (naive per-layer scale) gave mem ~900MB but p95 -> 120ms on 1-3 token batches, throughput ok for large batches.

josh: hmm that's big. did you use the INT8 decode kernel or the mixed FP8 fallback path?

eli: INT8 decode kernel. Also observed more KV cache misses due to quantization-induced small mismatches in key hashes (KV comparisons seem noisier). Misses cause extra fetch + dequantize path.

anika: can you paste the profiler snippet?

eli: pasted below — focus on the hot spots around KV lookup + dequantize:
```
Profile summary (small batch, 1-3 tokens):
- KV_lookup_int8: 34.2ms (46%)
- dequantize_kernel: 18.7ms (25%)
- attention_matmul: 12.1ms (16%)
- memcpy/dispatch: 6.8ms (9%)
- other: 1.2ms (4%)
```

sam: that dequantize_kernel is the killer for tiny batches. FP8 path kept everything fused so no separate dequantize.

maria: do we think the kernel selector is thrashing between int8 and fp8 depending on running batch distribution?

eli: yes — selector flips when batch_size >= 2 (old rule). With highly variable tail traffic, we spasm-switch and pay dequantize/reshape costs.

josh: propose hysteresis: only switch kernel if new mode persists for > 150ms or N consecutive requests. Also bias towards fused FP8 for <4 token batches to avoid dequantize overhead.

anika: agree. Also we should add a cheap online calibration check: if quant_scale_stddev across last 5 steps > threshold, avoid switching to INT8. That avoids noisier cache keys triggering miss storm.

eli: sketched rule I'm going to test:
```
if batch_size < 4:
    prefer = "fp8_fused"
else if recent_mode_stable_ms >= 150 and quant_scale_stddev < 0.01:
    prefer = "int8_compact"
else:
    prefer = current_mode
```

maria: curious about decode quality impact — any metric?

eli: ran QA eval on devset of 2k prompts: INT8 naive calibration dropped exact-match by ~0.9% and increased short hallucination tokens in long context. INT8 with per-layer calibration (better) reduced accuracy gap to ~0.2% but required extra calibration pass (30s per shard).

sam: tradeoffs: memory -45%, perf p95 worse for tiny batches unless hysteresis + fused fallback, quality slightly impacted unless extra calibration. Seems viable for Dedicated but risky for Hosted low-latency tails.

josh: action items:
- eli: land hysteresis + prefer-fused-for-small-batches patch (try on canary)
- anika: add quant_scale_stddev telemetry and per-layer calibration job as opt-in
- maria: run 24h canary traffic sim with realistic burstiness and check p50/p95/p99 + QA regression on rolling prompts

eli: started PR draft, linking perf traces: https://perf.internal/trace/1851234567

perf-ci: test run queued — will post perf diffs when done. :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks — nice triage. keep notes on memory wins per-shard and any decode regression severity so we can decide default for hosted API vs dedicated pools.

eli: will update thread with numbers after canary (ETA ~3h).
